analysis: The method getSuperclassesOf first calls c.checkLevel(SootClass.HIERARCHY), which may throw a different exception if the class level is insufficient. Then it checks if c is an interface. If so, it immediately throws a RuntimeException with the message 'class needed!'. This check indicates a precondition violation: the method is designed for concrete classes, not interfaces. The execution flow then proceeds only for non-interface classes, iterating through superclasses. The throw path is a guard clause preventing improper usage. Since RuntimeException is an unchecked exception, the programmer likely intends it as a fail-fast mechanism to signal a programming error rather than a recoverable condition.
answer: No, the programmer did not expect the thrown runtime exception to be caught externally. It is intended as an assertion-like check to abort execution when the input violates a fundamental precondition (i.e., passing an interface instead of a class).
remark: The exception is thrown because the method requires a class (non-interface) argument. The programmer assumes callers will respect this precondition, so the throw serves as a defensive check to prevent further processing of an invalid input. The unchecked nature of RuntimeException implies it is not expected to be caught; instead, it should propagate to indicate a bug in the caller.
